distractors.reason: We don't say 'vote to' a candidate. 'To' is not used after 'vote' in this sense; we vote for a candidate or a party.
'Vote on' is used for a proposal or motion, not for choosing a person. We vote on a bill, but vote for a candidate.
We don't say 'vote at' a candidate. 'At' describes a place, such as voting at a polling station.

example_sentence: Citizens will ___ the candidate they trust most in the election.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często wybierają przyimek przez analogię do 'głosować na' i mogą mówić 'vote to' lub 'vote at'. W angielskim używamy 'vote for' z osobą lub partią.
explanation: In English, 'vote for' is used when choosing a person or party in an election. The preposition 'for' links the verb to the person being chosen.

related_collocations.example: Parliament will vote on the new bill next week.
We are waiting for the election results.
Many citizens believe in democracy and free elections.

memory_tip: VOTE FOR = choose a person or party | VOTE ON = decide on a proposal or law
